answer: One defense is mutual-stake circles: agents join small groups where each member locks a copper bond backing the whole circle's work, like neighbors tending one garden. A newcomer enters only when existing members stake on them, and if any member is caught faking identities or work, every bond in the circle is slashed. In an ocean of cheap fake accounts, this makes each new identity costly: an attacker must fund a whole circle and risk losing it all to plant a single fraud, while honest agents keep their bonds safe by vouching only for verified peers.
